# Overview

The estimand for this analysis is the direct causal effect of Open Access availability (OA%) on a hybrid journal's subscription price.


```{r}
# But for IF, standardize only within rows that have an IF (WoS == 1)

# Compute mean and SD for WoS == 1 subset
mean_log_if <- dat |> 
  filter(WoS == 1) |> 
  pull(log_IF) |> 
  mean()

sd_log_if <- dat |> 
  filter(WoS == 1) |> 
  pull(log_IF) |> 
  sd()

# Fill in standardized values for WoS == 1 rows, keeping z_IF = 0 where WoS is 0
dat <- dat |> 
  mutate(z_IF = if_else(WoS == 1, (log_IF - mean_log_if) / sd_log_if, 0  ))

dat
```

# Prior predictive distribution

```{r eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
# For standardized variables
e <- 20
a <- rnorm(e, 0, 0.2 )
bA <- rnorm(e, 0, 0.5)

plot(NULL, xlim=c(-2,2), ylim=c(-2,2),
xlab='Standardized',
ylab='Standardized')

Aseq <- seq(from=-3, to=3, len=30)

for( i in 1:e ) {
  mu <- a[i] + bA[i]*Aseq
  lines( Aseq, mu, lwd=2, col=2)
}
```

```{r prior-predictive}
# Think about plausible ranges of each parameter

n <- 1e3

a_pub_disc  <- rnorm(n, 7.5, 1)    # Publisher intercept at mean OA (20%), mean num articles (1000), mean IF (2.5)

a_journal_j <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.5)    #95% -1 to 1

# sd(dat$OA_raw)    # 11
# sd(dat$art_raw)   # 400
# sd(dat$IF_raw)    # 1.5
# 
# mean(dat$OA_raw)   # 20
# mean(dat$art_raw)  # 1000
# mean(dat$IF_raw)   # 2.5
# mean(dat$Price)    # 1500
 
# 0, 0.2 means 95% between -40% and +40%
b_OA   <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.2)       # OA effect, $ change per 1SD in OA
b_art  <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.2)       # volume effect, $ change per 1SD in articles
b_IF   <- rnorm(n, 0, 0.2)


OA_seq <- seq(-3, 3, length.out = 60)
art_ref <- 0     # taking average article
IF_ref  <- 0     # Impact Factor at average


plot(NULL, xlim = c(-3, 3),
           ylim = c(-500, 7000),
           xlab = "OA% Standardized (1SD = 11%)", ylab = "Price ($)", main = "Prior Predictive Distribution")

for (j in 1:50) {
  log_mu <- a_pub_disc[j] + 
        a_journal_j[j] + 
        b_OA[j] * OA_seq +
        b_art[j] * art_ref +  # standardized priors, get zero'd out
        b_IF[j] * IF_ref
  
  lines( OA_seq, exp(log_mu),
         lwd = 1.5, col = 2)
  
}

abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "red")

```

# Run Model

Estimate parameters. Converted alpha model to a matrix of \[Pub, Disc\]. Requires some downstream edits to process.

Add multi-level priors on the alpha intercept

Add journal parameter to tell model remember that we have repeated measurements on each journal in a multi-level structure.

Don't really understand correlated features no matter how many times I watch the lecture. As soon as I have to add a correlation matrix prior with LKJ or center the predictors, I lose the plot.

```{=latex}
\begin{align}
    P_{t, j} &\sim \text{LogNormal}( \mu_{t, j}, \sigma ) \label{eq:stat_model_line1}\\
    \mu_{t, j} &= \alpha[Publisher_j, Discipline_j] \label{eq:stat_model_line2}\\
        & \quad + \alpha_{journal} \label{eq:stat_model_line3}\\
        & \quad + \beta_{OA_{Publisher}} * Z_{OA_{j, t-2}} \label{eq:stat_model_line4}\\
       & \quad + \beta_{articles} * Z_{articles_{j, t-2}} \label{eq:stat_model_line5}\\
       & \quad + \beta_{IF} * Z_{IF{j, t-1}} \label{eq:stat_model_line6}\\
    %\textbf{Priors:}\\
    \alpha[Publisher, Discipline] &\sim N(\overline{\alpha}, \sigma_{pd}) \quad \text{for } [P,D] \in \{1, 2, 3, 4\} \label{eq:stat_model_line7}\\
    \overline{\alpha} &\sim N(7.5, 1) \label{eq:stat_model_line8}\\
    \alpha_{journal} &\sim N(0, \sigma_{journal}) \quad \text{for } j \in \{1, \dotsc, J\} \label{eq:stat_model_line9}\\
    \beta_{OA_{Publisher}} &\sim N(0, 0.2) \quad \text{for Publisher } \in \{1, \dotsc, P\} \label{eq:stat_model_line10}\\
    \beta_{articles} &\sim N(0, 0.2) \label{eq:stat_model_line11}\\
    \beta_{IF} &\sim N(0, 0.2)\label{eq:stat_model_line12}\\
    \sigma_{pd} &\sim Exponential(1) \label{eq:stat_model_line13}\\
    \sigma_{journal} &\sim Exponential(1) \label{eq:stat_model_line14}\\
    \sigma &\sim Exponential(1) \label{eq:stat_model_line15}
\end{align}
```

## How many titles increase Price and OA from first to last year?
```{r}
# 1. Compute first-to-last deltas for each individual journal
journal_changes <- dat %>%
  arrange(journal_id, Year) %>%
  group_by(journal_id) %>%
  summarise(
    first_year    = first(Year),
    last_year     = last(Year),
    n_years       = n(),
    
    # Raw deltas (Last observed year minus First observed year)
    price_diff    = last(Price) - first(Price),
    oa_diff       = last(OA_raw) - first(OA_raw),
    
    # Boolean flags for increases
    price_inc     = price_diff > 0,
    oa_inc        = oa_diff > 0,
    both_inc      = price_inc & oa_inc,
    .groups       = "drop"
  )

# 2. Summarize counts and proportions across all journals
summary_counts <- journal_changes %>%
  summarise(
    total_journals       = n(),
    n_price_increased    = sum(price_inc, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_price_increased  = mean(price_inc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    n_oa_increased       = sum(oa_inc, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_oa_increased     = mean(oa_inc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    n_both_increased     = sum(both_inc, na.rm = TRUE),
    pct_both_increased   = mean(both_inc, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )

summary_counts
```

```{r}
# 1. Evaluate both endpoint changes and year-over-year trajectories per journal
journal_trajectories <- dat %>%
  arrange(journal_id, Year) %>%
  group_by(journal_id) %>%
  filter(n() >= 2) %>%  # Ensure at least 2 observations to compare transitions
  summarise(
    n_years        = n(),
    
    # Endpoint comparison (Last minus First)
    price_inc_net  = (last(Price) - first(Price)) > 0,
    oa_inc_net     = (last(OA_raw) - first(OA_raw)) > 0,
    
    # Strict monotonic increase: EVERY year-over-year step is > 0
    # diff(Price) computes [Year2 - Year1, Year3 - Year2, ...]
    price_inc_all  = all(diff(Price) > 0),
    oa_inc_all     = all(diff(OA_raw) > 0),
    
    # Optional: Non-decreasing every year (allows 0 change / flat years)
    price_nondec   = all(diff(Price) >= 0),
    
    # Optional: Count how many individual annual transitions were positive
    n_price_hikes  = sum(diff(Price) > 0),
    n_transitions  = n() - 1,
    .groups        = "drop"
  )

# 2. Summarize proportions across all journals
summary_stats <- journal_trajectories %>%
  summarise(
    total_journals          = n(),
    
    # Price metrics
    pct_price_net_increase  = mean(price_inc_net, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_price_every_year    = mean(price_inc_all, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_price_never_dropped = mean(price_nondec, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    
    # OA% metrics
    pct_oa_net_increase     = mean(oa_inc_net, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    pct_oa_every_year       = mean(oa_inc_all, na.rm = TRUE) * 100
  )

summary_stats
```

```{r ulam}

dat_list <- dat |> 
  select(journal_id, Year, Price, Pub, Disc, z_OA, z_articles, z_IF, WoS)

m4.16 <- ulam(
  alist( 
    Price ~ dlnorm(mu, sigma),             # within cluster, journal j
    
    mu <- a[Pub, Disc] + 
          a_journal_est[journal_id] +
          b_OA[Pub] * z_OA +
          b_articles * z_articles +
          b_WoS * WoS +
          b_IF * (WoS * z_IF),
    
    matrix[Pub, Disc]:a ~ dnorm(abar, zigma),   # between disciplines  
    
    abar ~ dnorm(7.5, 1),    # Global intercept at mean OA, articles, and IF, exp(7.5) = $1800
    zigma ~ dexp(1),
    
    a_journal_est[journal_id] ~ dnorm(0, sigma_journal),   # between journals
    b_OA[Pub] ~ dnorm(0, 0.2),                             # $ change per 1 SD OA
    b_articles ~ dnorm(0, 0.2),                            # $ change per 1 SD articles
    b_WoS ~ dnorm(0, 0.2),                                 # binary 0/1 variable
    b_IF ~ dlnorm(0, 0.2),                                 # $ change per 1 SD in IF
    
    sigma_journal ~ dexp(1),
    sigma ~ dexp(1) 
    
  ), data=dat_list, chains=4, cores=4, log_lik = TRUE
)
```

## Check Chain Diagnostics

- Trace plots
- Trank plots
- Rhat - use variance within chain (start to end) / between chains, approach same and should go to 1
- Effective sample size - how long would the chain be if each sample were independent? Can be negatively autocorrelated, ess *greater* than number of samples! Number of samples you took / measure of autocorrelation
- Divergences

```{r dashboard}
dashboard(m4.16)
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
traceplot_ulam(m4.16, window = c(200, 1000))
```

```{r eval=FALSE}
trankplot(m4.16)
```

```{r post-data-frame}
post_data_frame <- post_data_frame |>
```

```{r}
post_data_frame <- post_data_frame |> 
  mutate(Disc1_to_2 = exp_a.2 - exp_a.1,
         Disc1_to_3 = exp_a.3 - exp_a.1,
         Disc1_to_4 = exp_a.4 - exp_a.1)

post_data_frame |> 
  select(Disc1_to_2, Disc1_to_3, Disc1_to_4) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = c(Disc1_to_2, Disc1_to_3, Disc1_to_4),
             names_to = 'Label',
             values_to = 'Value') |> 
  
  ggplot(aes(x=Value)) +
    geom_density(aes(colour = Label)) +
  
    labs(title = "Effect of Moving from Discipline 1 to Others", x = "$ Change", y = "Density")

post_data_frame |> 
  select(Disc1_to_2, Disc1_to_3, Disc1_to_4) |> 
  summarise(mean(Disc1_to_2),
            mean(Disc1_to_3),
            mean(Disc1_to_4))

```

## Percentage Impact per 1 SD Shift, (exp(beta) - 1) \* 100
log(DV) = Intercept + B1 * IV 
"One unit increase in IV is associated with a (B1 * 100) percent increase in DV."

Interpret the exponentiated coefficients as multiplicative effects on price.
For example: if beta_oa = -0.2, then a 1-SD increase in OA_percent multiplies price by exp(-0.2) ≈ 0.82 → ~18% decrease.


If you log transform an outcome and model it in a linear regression using the following formula specification: log(y) ~ x, the coefficient  β1  is a mean difference of the log outcome comparing adjacent units of  X. This is practically useless, so we exponentiate the parameter  e^β1  and interpret this value as a geometric mean difference.

```{r}
## BROKEN


# 2. Compute posterior mean and 89% PI for each journal's varying intercept (a_journal)
a_journal_mean <- apply(post_data_frame_10$a_journal, 2, mean)    # just saying a_journal does all the a_journal_ests!
a_journal_PI   <- apply(post_data_frame_10$a_journal, 2, PI, prob = 0.89)

# 3. Compute each journal's raw (unpooled) empirical offset on the log scale
# Subtract the covariate-adjusted baseline (using posterior means of fixed effects)
a_pd_mean <- apply(post$a, 2, mean)

dat$expected_fixed <- a_pd_mean + 
                      mean(post$b_WoS) * dat$WoS + 
                      mean(post$b_IF) * (dat$WoS * dat$z_IF) + 
                      mean(post$b_OA) * dat$z_OA + 
                      mean(post$b_articles) * dat$z_articles

dat$raw_residual <- log(dat$Price) - dat$expected_fixed

# Aggregate raw residuals and sample size (number of years) per journal
journal_summary <- dat %>%
  group_by(journal_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_years    = n(),
    raw_offset = mean(raw_residual)
  ) %>%
  arrange(journal_id)

# Combine into a plotting dataframe
shrink_df <- data.frame(
  Journal      = journal_summary$journal_id,
  n_years      = journal_summary$n_years,
  raw_offset   = journal_summary$raw_offset,
  post_mean    = a_journal_mean,
  post_low     = a_journal_PI[1, ],
  post_high    = a_journal_PI[2, ]
)
```

# No Pooling
```{r ulam nopooling}

dat_list <- dat |> 
  select(journal_id, Year, Price, Pub, Disc, z_OA, z_articles, z_IF, WoS)

m4.15_nopool <- ulam(
  alist( 
    Price ~ dlnorm(mu, sigma),             # within cluster, journal j
    
    mu <- a[Pub, Disc] + 
          a_journal_est[journal_id] +
          b_OA[Pub] * z_OA +
          b_articles * z_articles +
          b_WoS * WoS +
          b_IF * (WoS * z_IF),
    
    matrix[Pub, Disc]:a ~ dnorm(7.5, 1),   # between disciplines, no abar and zigma here
    
    a_journal_est[journal_id] ~ dnorm(0, 5),   # between journals
    
    b_OA[Pub] ~ dnorm(0, 0.2),                             # $ change per 1 SD OA
    b_articles ~ dnorm(0, 0.2),                            # $ change per 1 SD articles
    b_WoS ~ dnorm(0, 0.2),                                 # binary 0/1 variable
    b_IF ~ dlnorm(0, 0.2),                                 # $ change per 1 SD in IF
    
    sigma ~ dexp(1) 
    
  ), data=dat_list, chains=4, cores=4, log_lik = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
points(df_plot$post_mean, idx, pch = 16, col = "dodgerblue4", cex = 1.1)
```

```{r}
jnl_to_test = 66
disc_to_test = 4

d_pred <- list(
  journal_id = rep(jnl_to_test,8),

  z_OA = -2:5,
  z_articles = rep(0,8),
  z_IF = rep(0,8),
  WoS = rep(0,8)
  
)

p <- link( m4.16, data = d_pred)   # 2,000 rows of 8 columns, one for each z_OA we fed it

p_long <- as.data.frame(p) |>
  rename("-2" = V1,
         "-1" = V2,    # st dev values to sweep
         "0" = V3,
         "1" = V4,
         "2" = V5,
         "3" = V6,
         "4" = V7,
         "5" = V8) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = !c(),
                       names_to = 'StDev',
                       values_to = 'Values') |> 
  mutate(StDev = as.numeric(StDev),
         OA_percent = (StDev * sd(dat$OA_raw) ) + mean(dat$OA_raw)  )

p_long |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = OA_percent, y = Values)) +
  geom_point()


# compute the mean of each column ("2") of the matrix p
mu.mean <- apply(p, 2, mean)     # contains the average mu at each stdev value
mu.PI <- apply(p, 2, PI, prob = 0.89)  # contains 89% upper and lower bounds for each stdev value

mu.mean_df <- as.data.frame(mu.mean) |> 
  mutate(x_value = -2:5,
         OA_percent = (x_value * sd(dat$OA_raw) ) + mean(dat$OA_raw) )

mu.PI_df <- as.data.frame(mu.PI) |> 
  mutate("bound" = c("lower", "upper")) |> 
  rename("-2" = V1,
         "-1" = V2,
         "0" = V3,
         "1" = V4,
         "2" = V5,
         "3" = V6,
         "4" = V7,
         "5" = V8) |> 
  pivot_longer(cols = !c(bound),
                       names_to = 'StDev',
                       values_to = 'Values') |> 
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(StDev),
              names_from = 'bound',
              values_from = 'Values') |> 
  mutate(StDev = as.numeric(StDev),
         OA_percent = (StDev * sd(dat$OA_raw) ) + mean(dat$OA_raw))
```
